article_text:
国立新美術館で12月13日まで開催中の「ルーヴル美術館展 ルネサンス」。会期末の混雑対策として、12月7日（月）～13日（日）は日時指定制が導入されます。日時指定券は10月31日（土）12：00から、アソビュー！（オンラインチケット）で販売予定です。 前売券・当日券は12月6日（日）までの有効期限となりますのでご注意ください。

※中学生以下の方（保護者の方は日時指定券が必要）、 障害者手帳をご持参の方（付添の方1名含む）、無料観覧券をお持ちの方は、 日時指定券の購入は不要です。

詳しくは、本展公式サイトをご覧ください。 https://www.ntv.co.jp/louvre2026/ticket/

（読売新聞美術展ナビ編集班）

「ルーヴル美術館展 ルネサンス」

会期：2026年9月9日（水）～12月13日（日） 【日時指定期間】12月7日（月）～13日（日）

会場： 国立新美術館 企画展示室１E（ 東京都港区六本木7-22-2 ）

開館時間：10:00～18:00 ※毎週金・土曜日は20:00まで ※入場は閉館の30分前まで

観覧料： 一般2,400円、大学生1,400円、高校生1,000円

休館日：毎週火曜日 ※ただし11月3日（火･祝）、12月8日（火）は開館、11月4日（水）は休館

アクセス： 東京メトロ千代田線乃木坂駅6出口直結

詳しくは 展覧会公式ウェブサイト へ。

title_original: Artists Equity’s Amy Baer on Building a Sustainable Indie Model with Movies That Don’t Star Matt Damon or Ben Affleck
editorial_title_zh: Artists Equity的艾米·贝尔谈如何用不以马特·达蒙或本·阿弗莱克为主演的电影打造可持续的独立模式
editorial_excerpt_zh: 这家制作公司的电影和电视部门总裁探讨了新成立的Artists Equity独立电影公司（Artists Equity Independent Pictures），以及如何将他们独特的模式应用于中小成本电影。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "人们可能依然很难确切理解本·阿弗莱克与马特·达蒙的Artists Equity究竟是一家什么样的公司，或者它是如何运作的。有时，就连公司自己的高管也很难说清楚究竟是什么赋予了这家公司独特的秘诀。", "links": [{"text": "Ben Affleck", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/ben-affleck/"}, {"text": "Matt Damon", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/matt-damon/"}, {"text": "Artists Equity", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/artists-equity/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我想人们正开始理解它，但我认为大家并未真正明白这家公司的雄心和体量，”Artists Equity电影与电视总裁、同时也是马特和本的二把手埃米·贝尔（Amy Baer）在接受IndieWire采访时表示。", "links": [{"text": "Amy Baer", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/amy-baer/"}, {"text": "film", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/film/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她继续说道：“它的存在是为了赋能并保护视觉叙事的艺术。（达蒙和阿弗莱克）深深扎根于电影历史之中。他们都是影迷，充满热情的影迷，不仅希望重新定义台前幕后创意人员的报酬方式——这显然是我们公司的基础组成部分，即股权部分——还要确保我们正在创造一个良性循环，以便它能够持久发展。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Screen-Shot-2026-09-07-at-5.18.25-PM.png?w=300&h=168&crop=1", "alt": "'Musk'", "caption": "", "credit": "IndieWire", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/PatrickStewartObituary.jpg?w=300&h=168&crop=1", "alt": "patrick stewart obituary", "caption": "", "credit": "IndieWire", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但贝尔觉得，随着该公司全新独立厂牌Artists Equity Independent Pictures（简称AEIP）的推出，她向外界解释Artists Equity模式的工作变得稍微轻松了一些。该厂牌将由曾任Topic Studios实体制作高管的詹妮弗·韦斯廷（Jennifer Westin）领导并向贝尔汇报，它将采用让Artists Equity的《AIR》、《绝命缉毒》（The Rip）、《动物》（Animals）和《引爆者》（The Instigators）得以问世的同款财务模式。通过要求演职人员实际投资并持有电影股权，他们在前期可以拿到较少的片酬，但能在电影成功后获得更好的后端收益。", "links": [{"text": "The Rip", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/the-rip/"}, {"text": "Animals", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/news/breaking-news/ben-affleck-direct-matt-damon-netflix-crime-thriller-animals-1234948415/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "贝尔说：“这就是独立电影的模式，对吧？我当了14年独立制片人。我制作的每部电影中，所有参与者都在前期拿了较少的报酬，以帮助电影得以拍成。在典型的独立电影中，50%的份额归电影创作团队，另外50%归出资方。我们只是对创意团队说：‘这是你们的份额，你们自己分吧。’我们不会告诉你们该怎么做。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/GettyImages-2256165201.jpg?w=650", "alt": "纽约，纽约 - 1月13日：（左起）蒂姆·韦耶斯、艾莉森·温特、克莱门廷·卡拉韦、吉吉·富凯、菲利普·古尔、狄龙·韦斯特、露安娜·巴罗斯·达蒙、马特·达蒙、本·阿弗莱克、凯伦·威拉曼、蔡·卡特、凯文·霍拉兰、萨沙·委内瑞亚诺和艾米·贝尔于2026年1月13日在纽约市爱丽丝·图利音乐厅出席《绝命缉毒》世界首映礼。（罗伊·罗克林/Netflix盖蒂图片社 摄）", "caption": "艾米·贝尔（最右）出席在纽约举行的《绝命缉毒》首映礼，图为Netflix供图盖蒂图片社", "credit": "IndieWire", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对于Artists Equity旗下的独立项目而言，这种模式意味着能够争取到平时可能不会接受低片酬的高端剪辑师、作曲家或明星。贝尔认为，这与多年来服务于独立电影的模式如出一辙，只是在某些地方做了一些加码。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "AEIP厂牌下的首个项目是《太阳之女》（A Woman in the Sun），由《你的一生》（Love of Your Life）和《奈德》（Nyad）的编剧朱莉娅·考克斯（Julia Cox）编剧并执导，由蕾妮·齐薇格、茜茜·斯派塞克和米娅·特里普雷顿主演。Black Bear已确定担任发行商。刚刚宣布的项目还有萨姆·琼斯（Sam Jones）执导的《下游》（Downriver），将由加内特·赫德兰、杰克·莱西和杰西卡·贝尔主演。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "贝尔表示，该厂牌不限类型，但也不会去拍低成本的砍杀恐怖片或实验电影，而是寻找那些有潜力突围、且拥有明确受众基础的高水准且具商业潜力的独立电影明珠。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "AEIP将寻找现成的项目包进行合作，而不是在内部进行开发，随后与电影人一起确定初始预算，并识别新锐人才——无论是首次执导的导演还是第五次执导的导演。贝尔表示，这家厂牌最忌讳的就是手里有钱就乱花，所以在早期阶段，各项决策将会非常审慎。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但该厂牌的建立是基于达蒙和阿弗莱克的信念：有许多电影理应获得拍摄的机会，但不应该为了获得融资而必须依赖2000块银幕的排片承诺。而且有马特和本为这些电影保驾护航，自然也大有裨益。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "贝尔说：“（我们的想法是）真正开始在这样一个庇护伞下支持下一代导演和编导，它具有强大的实力，能够在营销、发行、宣传甚至某种程度的项目打包方面闯过重重关卡。他们两人坐在厂牌的最高层，赋予了它一种我认为我们公司非常独一无二的分量。外面有很多非常优秀的独立电影公司，但我觉得没有哪一家有两位奥斯卡得主坐在最高层。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "AEIP电影与旗舰Artists Equity厂牌旗下电影的一个重要区别在于，这些独立电影将不受AE任何发行协议的约束，包括用于流媒体的Netflix协议以及用于院线的索尼影视协议。这两项协议都要求最低预算水平，而AEIP电影的预算通常会低于这一标准。如果Netflix或索尼极其喜爱某部作品，它们依然可以买下。", "links": [{"text": "Sony Pictures for theatrical", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/news/breaking-news/ben-affleck-matt-damon-artists-equity-overall-deal-sony-1235135502/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/RIP_20241202_WP_06568_R3.jpg?w=650", "alt": "《绝命缉毒》。（左起）马特·达蒙饰戴恩·杜马斯中尉，本·阿弗莱克饰J·D·伯恩警探。摄影：沃里克·佩奇/Netflix © 2025。", "caption": "《绝命缉毒》沃里克·佩奇/Netflix", "credit": "IndieWire", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不过，与那些更大预算的项目一样，如果电影在流媒体上达到特定的观看量门槛，AEIP电影仍然有资格获得绩效奖金。《绝命缉毒》就是这种情况，Artists Equity向该片全部1,200名剧组成员支付了一定比例的薪酬奖金。贝尔没有透露这些观看量门槛是多少，也没有透露个人获得了多少奖金，只是表示观看量“非常可观”，奖金“相当丰厚”。", "links": [{"text": "The Rip", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/criticism/movies/the-rip-netflix-movie-review-ben-affleck-matt-damon-1235173331/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "AEIP需要具备预算意识，并对每部电影的受众有清醒的认知。在圣丹斯电影节首映、由詹妮弗·洛佩兹（Jennifer Lopez）主演的音乐剧翻拍片《蜘蛛女之吻》（Kiss of the Spider Woman）票房惨败，在3000万美元预算的背景下仅收获180万美元票房。这部电影在贝尔上任之前就已存在，但它同样是一个教训，让人必须看清市场传递的信息。", "links": [{"text": "Kiss of the Spider Woman", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/news/trailers/kiss-of-the-spider-woman-trailer-jennifer-lopez-1235146303/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "贝尔提醒说，尽管达蒙和阿弗莱克如今星光熠熠，但他们有着真正的独立电影根基，曾在90年代与凯文·史密斯（Kevin Smith）四处奔走，极力争取任何拍摄机会。她认为Artists Equity与MRC、Fifth Season甚至A24的不同之处在于，这是一家由两位一线巨星领导的公司，他们对待首席执行官和首席创意官职务的态度，与对待表演、编剧或导演一样严肃。", "translated": article_text:
It can still be a struggle for people to grasp exactly what Ben Affleck and Matt Damon ‘s Artists Equity banner is all about or how it works. In some cases it’s even hard for its own leaders to articulate what gives the company its secret sauce.

“I think they’re beginning to understand it, but I think that people don’t really understand the ambition and scope of this business,” Amy Baer , Artists Equity’s president of film and television and the No. 2 to Matt and Ben, told IndieWire.

“It is existing to enable and preserve the art of visual storytelling,” she continued. “[Damon and Affleck] are deeply, deeply rooted in the history of film. They are cinephiles, both of them, passionate cinephiles who not only want to redefine how creatives — both in front of the camera and behind the camera — are compensated, which is obviously the foundational component of our company, the equity piece, but to also ensure that we are creating a virtuous cycle so that it can endure.”

But Baer feels her job in explaining the Artists Equity model to people just got a little easier with the launch of the company’s new independent label, Artists Equity Independent Pictures (AEIP). The label, which will be led by former Topic Studios physical production exec Jennifer Westin as reporting to Baer, will use the same financial model that has allowed films like Artists Equity’s “Air,” “ The Rip ,” “ Animals ,” and “The Instigators” to get made. By asking talent to actually invest and take equity in the film, they take a smaller fee up front but can receive a better backend in the film’s success.

“That is the indie model, right? I spent 14 years as an independent producer. Everyone involved in every movie I made took less up front in order to help get the movie made,” Baer said. “In a typical indie film, 50 percent of the points go to the filmmaking team, the other 50 percent go to the financiers. We just say to the creative team, ‘Here’s your points. Carve it up.’ We’re not going to tell you how to do it.”

For an independent project under Artists Equity, that model can mean being able to secure a higher end editor, composer, or star who might not normally work for less. Baer views it as the same model that has served independent film for years, but with a few sweeteners in certain places.

The first project under the AEIP banner is “A Woman in the Sun,” which is written and directed by “Love of Your Life” and “Nyad” screenwriter Julia Cox and stars Renée Zellweger, Sissy Spacek, and Mia Threapleton. Black Bear is already set up as a distributor. Also just announced was Sam Jones’ “Downriver,” which will star Garrett Hedlund, Jake Lacy, and Jessica Biel.

Baer says the label is genre agnostic, but it’s not going for low budget slasher horror or experimental films, rather elevated, yet still commercial indie gems that have the potential to break out and have a clear audience in front of them.

AEIP is going to be searching for packaged projects rather than developing internally, then working with filmmakers to set an initial budget, and to identify emerging talent, be they first-time directors or fifth-timers. Baer says the worst thing this label can do is to spend money just because they have it, so things will be very judicious in the early days.

But the label was built on Damon and Affleck’s belief that there are a lot of movies that deserve a shot to get made but that shouldn’t have to rely on a 2000-screen commitment in order to even get financing. And having Matt and Ben championing those films doesn’t hurt.

“[The idea is] to really start to support the next generation of directors and writer-directors under an auspice that has the heft of being able to run the gauntlet on the marketing, distribution, promotion, and even in the packaging to a certain extent,” Baer said. “To have the two of them sitting atop the label gives a heft that I think is very unique to our company. There’s plenty of really good independent film companies out there, but I don’t think any of them have two Oscar winners sitting on top of it.”

One important distinction between AEIP movies and those under the flagship Artists Equity banner is that the indies won’t be bound by either of AE’s output deals, including Netflix for streaming and Sony Pictures for theatrical . Both of those deals require minimum budget levels that AEIP movies will typically be beneath. Netflix or Sony can still buy one if they love it.

Like those bigger budget projects though, AEIP movies will still qualify for performance bonuses if the film reaches certain viewership thresholds on streaming. That was the case with “ The Rip ,” in which Artists Equity paid out a percentage of the salary for each of the 1,200 crew members on the film. Baer didn’t disclose what those viewership thresholds were or how much individuals got paid in bonuses except to say it was “robust” views and a “substantial” bonus.

AEIP will need to be budget conscious and acutely aware of the audience for any of its films. “ Kiss of the Spider Woman ,” a musical remake starring Jennifer Lopez that premiered at Sundance, flopped hard with just $1.8 million at the box office against a $30 million budget. That movie predated Baer, but it’s a teaching moment all the same to be clear on what the market is telling you.

Baer reminds though that for all their star power today, Damon and Affleck have true indie roots, running around with Kevin Smith in the ’90s trying to get any shot they could. What she believes sets Artists Equity apart from the likes of MRC, Fifth Season, or even A24 is that they’re a company led by two A-listers who take the CEO and chief creative officer role as seriously as they do acting, writing, or directing.

“I think people really underestimate the ambition of the company. This is not a talent production company on steroids,” Baer said. “They both take that job incredibly seriously and are committed to being as nimble and as forward-facing as possible to make sure that the thing they love doing the most endures.”

The one thing Baer says is not part of her mandate is finding projects for Matt and Ben, who need no help with that. So it’s pretty unlikely that Affleck or Damon would actually star in one of these indies themselves, but they won’t be far away.

“They’re very disciplined about where they’re going to spend their time and energy, and they don’t want to leverage it just for the sake of getting things made. They want to empower other people to get things made,” Baer said. “It’s something that other companies can’t necessarily offer because those guys will get attention when they decide that they’re going to go help promote one of our films. What’s been really evident is that they’re very disciplined about we’re not going to make this and do that supporting role just so that we can justify making it. They want these things to stand on their own two feet.”
excerpt_original: The production label's president of film and TV discusses the newly-launched Artists Equity Independent Pictures and how to apply their unique model to smaller films.

article_text:
Just a week ago, “ Clayface ” was expected to easily top the box office, with opening weekend projections of $25 million to $35 million from 3,400 North American theaters. (Rivals suggest a slightly softer debut around $22 million to $28 million). Now, Warner Bros. and DC’s R-rated comic book adaptation might face some unexpected competition for No. 1 from A24’s buzzy Elizabeth Holmes documentary “ You Can See Everything .”

“You Can See Everything” could collect a staggering $20 million to $25 million while expanding to 2,600 venues in its second weekend of release. It would be the rare film to see an increase in ticket sales in its sophomore outing. The stranger-than-fiction film, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, shattered initial expectations with $15.6 million from just 855 theaters, marking the biggest opening for a nonmusical documentary in 20 years. It has earned $20.8 million domestically to date.

Related Stories

'KPop Demon Hunters,' 'Squid Game' Stars Fete Netflix's Korea Decade as Ted Sarandos Teases 'Tantara,' 'All of Us Are Dead' Season 2

Netflix Sets Release Date for Rob Lowe Documentary 'The Outsider’

Whether or not “Clayface” winds up in first place on domestic charts, the movie seems well positioned theatrically. It’s aiming for $20 million to $25 million overseas from 76 markets for a global tally of $45 million to $55 million. The film cost $44 million to produce, a fraction of the budget of DC’s recent adaptations including this July’s “Supergirl” and 2025’s “Superman.” After “Superman” successfully reset the languishing DC Universe, “Supergirl” bombed with $126 million against a $170 million budget and marked a step back for the studio’s comic book ambitions. A body-horror thriller,” Clayface” is much darker than those family friendly adventures. Directed by James Watkins, “Clayface” follows the titular Batman villain, a rising movie star who volunteers for a highly experimental medical procedure after his face is severely disfigured.

“Clayface” is one of several new releases this weekend, including Black Bear’s offbeat romantic comedy “Wicker,” Laika’s stop-motion animated “Wildwood,” Sacha Baron Cohen’s mockumentary “Ali G: Who Iz I?” and the Jenna Ortega-led literary adaptation “Klara and the Sun.” Each of those movies are targeting single digit debuts.

“Wicker” is expected to earn $6 million to $8 million from 1,471 locations, a solid start for the low-budget indie. Olivia Colman stars as an ostracized woman who commissions a local basketmaker to weave her a husband. Her unexpected romance with the creation (Alexander Skarsgård) sparks jealousy in the village. Black Bear acquired the well-reviewed movie for $2.5 million after it generated buzz at Sundance Film Festival.

“Wildwood” is tracking a debut of $6 million to $8 million from more than 2,000 theaters. It’s the first release from Laika Studios since 2019’s “Missing Link,” which opened to $6 million from 3,413 theaters and ended its run with $26 million globally. Laika is best known for making the 2009 stop-motion fantasy “Coraline.” Stop-motion animation is labor intensive (this movie took more than five years to make), so “Wildwood” carries a substantial $100 million price tag and likely won’t turn a theatrical profit based on initial projections. Directed by Travis Knight, Laika’s CEO who directed this year’s flop “Masters of the Universe” for Amazon MGM, “Wildwood” revolves around a teenage girl who travels with a classmate into an enchanted forest after her brother is abducted. Reviews have been sterling, with Variety’s chief film critic Guy Lodge praising the movie as “Laika’s most ambitious feature to date” and noting the “lavish stop-motion spectacle makes it feel fresh and alive.”

“Klara and the Sun,” too, might struggle to connect with audiences. It’s estimated to open to $2 million from roughly 850 cinemas. Sony scaled back the theatrical footprint to a moderate release after reviews panned the movie as “ calamitous ” and “ confoundingly awful .” Sony produced the Taika Waititi-directed adaptation for a modest $20 million, so any box office losses won’t be too painful. Based on Kazuo Ishiguro’s 2021 novel, “Klara and the Sun” takes place in the dystopian future as an obsolete companion android (Jenna Ortega) tries to bond with her new owner, a young sick girl named Josie.

“Ali G: Who Iz I?” is only playing in 125 theaters for two days before moving to Prime Video on a to-be-determined date. Baron Cohen wrote, directed and stars in “Ali G,” based on his breakout character — a wannabe rapper — who originally appeared on Channel 4’s “The 11 O’Clock Show” and later on “Da Ali G Show” in the early 2000s. Much like the comedian’s prior work, including 2006’s “Borat” and 2020’s “Borat Subsequent Moviefilm,” the “Ali G” movie was shot in secret. Though plot details aren’t clear, Baron Cohen plays three characters in the film including the former Mossad agent from his Showtime series “Who Is America?”

秀吉の命令で秀長が築きはじめた

和歌山城（和歌山市）は徳川御三家のひとつ、紀州徳川家の城というイメージが強いが、創建したのは羽柴秀長である。天正 13 年（ 1585 ） 4 月、紀州攻略を終えた羽柴秀吉は、紀伊（和歌山県と三重県南西部）や和泉（大阪府南西部）の統治を弟の秀長にまかせることにし、紀州支配の拠点として紀ノ川下流域の南岸、吹上丘陵の北端部に位置する虎伏山（岡山）に築城させた。

その際、紀州攻略に携わったみずからの手勢 1 万人を秀長に預けているので、秀吉は力をかなり入れていたようだ。その手勢の半分は直後の四国征伐に動員されたが、残りの人員は残って、城の普請に携わったと思われる。

普請奉行を務めたのは藤堂高虎で、虎伏山の山頂部と山麓が整備されたようだ。虎伏山はラクダのこぶのように西峰と東峰に分かれ、現在、天守が建つのは西峰だが、創建当初は東峰に中枢が置かれた。また、大手門の位置は現在のように城の北東ではなかった。いま城の南西に岡口門があり、元和 7 年（ 1621 ）に建てられた櫓門が現存するが、ここに秀長時代の大手門があった。

天正 13 年に築城が開始されたのち、秀長は同年閏 8 月には大和郡山城（奈良県大和郡山市）に移り、その後は重臣の桑山重晴が城代を務め、秀長の死後も慶長 5 年（ 1600 ）の関ヶ原合戦まで、重晴が城主として城を整備した。

その当時、すなわち秀長と重晴の時代に築かれた石垣が、いまも和歌山城内には広範に残っている。その特徴は、紀州の「青石」と呼ばれる緑色片岩をふくむ結晶片岩を、ほとんど加工せずにもちいた野面積みであることだ。結晶片岩とは地下深いところで高い温度と圧力によって再結晶し、雲母などによる縞状の組織を持つようになった変成岩で、薄い板を貼り合わせたような形状なのですぐにわかる。

かなりの規模で残る秀長由来の石垣

結晶片岩が積まれているからといって、秀長と重晴の時代の石垣だと断定できるわけではないが、積み方からもこの時代のものと考えられる石垣は、かなり残っている。それを見ていきたい。この石垣は虎伏山の山裾から山頂にかけて、意外なほど広く分布している。

まず虎伏山の北東部。結晶片岩の野面積みによる石垣が山裾を覆うように積まれ、隅角部が 90 度を超えて広がった「しのぎ積み」と呼ばれる古い技法も見られる。

虎伏山北西部の鶴の渓と呼ばれる場所も、山裾が結晶片岩の野面積みの石垣で延々と支えられている。かなり大きな築石がゆるい勾配で積まれ、櫓台などの隅角部には、直方体の石の長辺と短辺を交互に積んで強度を得る算木積みがまだ発達していない。

このあたりの石垣は、勾配がゆるいうえに築石同士が密着していないので、簡単に登ることができそうに見えるが、ともかく、秀長と重晴の時代から、和歌山城はかなりの規模にわたって石垣で整備されていたことがわかる。

結晶片岩、わけても紀州の青石は、存在感が強い美しい石として知られ、各地の名庭にもよく置かれている。幾筋もの縞が通った青みがかった石は、実際、存在感があり、それが幾重にも積まれているのは壮観である。雨に濡れたときなどは独特の美しさがある。

本丸の天守台も最古の石垣だと考えられている。そこには昭和 20 年（ 1945 ） 7 月の空襲で焼失し、同 33 年（ 1958 ）に鉄筋コンクリート造で外観復元された天守が建つが、石垣は古い。

古い石垣で築造技術が未熟だったために平面がいびつで、したがって天守や連立する櫓の 1 階部分もいびつな形をしている。このため天守も、不当辺四角形の 1 階にほぼ正方形の 2 階が乗るという複雑な構造で、復元天守を設計した藤岡通夫氏は、 1 階と 2 階のバランスをとるのが非常に難しかったと回想している。

また、天守台は隅角部などに墓石などからの転用石が見られ、やはり秀長が整備した大和郡山城と共通している。秀長と重晴の時代に積まれた結晶片岩は、この虎伏山のほか、城の南東の天妃山という岩山（現・岡公園内）から切り出され、近くから石を切り出せない大和郡山城よりは条件がよかった。しかし、それでも大量に切り出した石材を遠方から運ぶシステムはまだ整っておらず、石が足りなくなって、寺院などからも運んできたということだろう。

ちなみに、秀長の時代は前述のように本丸御殿跡、すなわち虎伏山山頂の東峰が城の中心だったようで、ここからは天守がよく見える。

浅野期、徳川期の石垣との組み合わせの妙

天守から「表坂」を下る途中、本丸一ノ門の石垣も加工されていない結晶片岩が積まれている。ここの石垣を修復する際、裏込め石から宝篋印塔や石臼などの転用石がいくつも見つかったという。

秀長時代の石垣は、かつての大手門である岡口門の周辺でも見ることができる。岡口門の南側の南堀は秀長時代に整備されたと考えられる。大正 14 年（ 1925 ）に埋め立てられてしまったのだが、築造時に地盤が軟弱だったためだろう、まず低い石垣で護岸を固め、その上に高い石垣が築かれていた。この護岸を固めていた石垣が 2 段程度ではあるが、堀を埋めた土中からいまも顔を出している。

和歌山城は関ヶ原合戦後、その功によって浅野幸長が 37 万 6000 石で入封し、城を大改修して大手門の位置も替えた。そして元和 5 年（ 1619 ）、徳川家康の十男である頼宣が 55 万 5000 石をあたえられて城主になると、徳川家の城にふさわしく拡張と整備が重ねられた。

このため、ここまで紹介した秀長と桑山重晴に由来する石垣のほかに、浅野期の石垣、徳川期の石垣も見ることができる。新裏坂下の石垣などは、和泉砂岩が積まれた打ち込みハギで、浅野期に整備された。

一方、大手門から城内に入って次の門である中門跡や、虎伏山の南東部の松の丸櫓台などには、徳川期の 17 世紀後半から 18 世紀前半に築かれたと考えられる、整った切込ハギの石垣が見られる。中門の石垣には熊野産の花崗斑岩、松の丸櫓台は隅角部には花崗斑岩、ほかは和泉砂岩が積まれている。

こうしたあたらしい石垣が、秀長や重晴時代の石垣に継がれている箇所もあり、さまざまな石垣を比較できる。だが、そのなかでも秀長由来の石垣の存在感は大きい。それを存分に味わえる城である。

article_text:
Lionsgate and Steven Paul , an entrepreneur and film producer who has personally lobbied President Donald Trump on a federal tax incentive for Hollywood , are forming a joint venture through which Paul’s SP Media will make a “significant” investment in new initiatives together with Lionsgate.

Under the agreement, SP Media also will produce independent feature films that Lionsgate will distribute. The relationship will be managed through the joint venture, which will be majority owned and controlled by Lionsgate. The amount of Paul’s planned investment into the JV was not disclosed. It’s understood that the joint venture’s investments will be into new businesses that expand Lionsgate’s content, including the continued diversification of 3 Arts Entertainment, Lionsgate’s talent management and production division, into new areas like sports and influencers.

Related Stories

Sharjah Film Festival Partners With UAE's Media Authority in Push to Assist Emerging Filmmakers

Paul, who serves as chairman, founder and CEO of Crystal Sky Pictures and SP Media Group, has shepherded several box-office successes in years past, including the Baby Geniuses franchise, “Ghost Rider” and “Ghost Rider 2: Spirit of Vengeance” starring Nicolas Cage, “Ghost in the Shell” starring Scarlett Johansson, and the Lionsgate-distributed “Rambo: Last Blood.”

More recently, Paul has been working with actor Jon Voight to pitch Trump on a series of measures to help the U.S. entertainment industry, including a federal tax incentive for TV and film productions. At an Aug. 31 meeting at the White House , Paul cited his upcoming film about Richard Nixon’s early years — telling Trump the project would need to be produced overseas unless there is a viable U.S. tax incentive.

The announcement of the JV between Lionsgate and SP Media comes after a report last week that Legendary Entertainment revived its bid to acquire Lionsgate .

“Steven is a savvy and experienced entrepreneur who has a longstanding relationship with our studio, and I’m pleased to partner with him across multiple touchpoints of our business,” Lionsgate CEO Jon Feltheimer said in announcing the agreement. “He recognizes the unique and valuable assets that we have built and his investment will help drive the continued growth of these businesses.”

Paul said in a statement: “Lionsgate is one of the most dynamic and entrepreneurial content studios in the media space today. I’m delighted to build on my longstanding relationship with Jon Feltheimer and the Lionsgate leadership team as we grow our businesses together in an industry environment filled with opportunity.”

Paul’s SP Group of Companies has holdings in media, entertainment, talent representation, technology, hospitality, banking and real estate. The portfolio includes the Samuel Goldwyn Building in Century City; the Casa Marella Boutique Hotel in South Beach Miami; the JLTV television network; Atlas Comics (founded by Marvel Comics owner Martin Goodman); Avenue Six Studios in Van Nuys, California ; Echo Bridge Distribution Co.; and Hanks Café in Century City.

The deal was negotiated for Lionsgate by COO Brian Goldsmith, EVP and general counsel Bruce Tobey and senior VP of corporate development Suzy Felfeli and for SP Media by group president and COO Scott Karol. Moelis served as financial adviser to Lionsgate and Lazard served as financial adviser to SP Media. Law firm Paul Hastings repped SP Media on the deal.

Kathleen Kennedy, who served as the president of Lucasfilm from 2012 to 2026, helped organize a group of industry dignitaries to put together a framework for how Hollywood should talk about it.", "links": [{"text": "a group of industry dignitaries", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/biz/news/secret-hollywood-groups-ai-plan-protecting-copyrighted-work-1236840245/"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/AI-Movie-Dreams-of-Violets.jpg?w=1024", "alt": "", "caption": "From the AI-generated docudrama “Dreams of Violets” Courtesy of Dreams of Violets", "credit": "Variety · Film"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“When you have a set of tools that all of a sudden, ‘I can dream it, and I can create it, and I can show it to somebody,’ what you realize is that it heightens your creativity and did not diminish it at all,” Erwin says."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "But even with such attitudinal strides, Pew Research shows that people’s fears about AI’s societal impact are high, and digital choirs hurl insults at any project featuring the tech. article_text:
Manhattan Beach Studios in Southern California is a pinnacle of revolutionary technology, home to both the “volume” screens where Jon Favreau filmed the “Mandalorian” franchise and Lightstorm Entertainment, where James Cameron has spent years bringing the Na’vi to life.

Tucked away at Stage 21 lies Innovative Dreams, an AI offshoot of director Jon Erwin’s Entertainment company Wonder Project. Here, chief operating officer Bryan Yee sips from a Diet Coke can as he showcases the soundstage housing Innovative Dreams’ crown jewel: a collection of LED screens where a team of AI artists weaves generative AI into productions. It’s not the first time the space has been shown to a journalist. But that it’s happened multiple times this year shows that three-quarters of the way into 2026, AI is no longer Hollywood’s ultimate bad word.

Related Stories

Sony Pictures Television Hires Lauren Glaubach, Former YouTube and Pinterest Exec, to Lead Digital and Social Distribution Strategy

Belgian Series 'The Inheritance' Scores Sony Pictures Television Award at Rome’s MIA Market

The term “AI” has emerged as an addendum to the Hays Code, the 20th-century guidelines dictating what studios should and shouldn’t include in their films. It’s spooked the worlds of corporate and art alike, especially after months of headlines over the potentially world-ending nature of AI models and warnings that progress needs to be paced . Americans are also increasingly believing the tech is doing more harm than good, according to a recent Gallup poll .

But much like the way studios and directors of the 1960s and ’70s embraced the once-taboo profanity and nudity, this year AI has found a new wave of advocates eager to go public. The technology turned up at marquee film festivals, including Tribeca, which premiered the AI-generated docudrama “Dreams of Violets.” Oscar winner Reese Witherspoon declared that “the AI revolution has begun,” and Martin Scorsese said filmmakers had to be “open to how [film] can evolve.” George Lucas was perhaps the most blunt in a July interview: “There’s nothing you can do about it.”

Part of what’s spurred this breakthrough involves creatives getting to know the technology. Some have found it additive to their projects: Veteran producer Ryan Kavanaugh says his firm, Acme Studios, lowered the cost of Doug Liman’s film “Bitcoin” from $200 million to $70 million with the use of AI. Below-the-line costs on “Bitcoin” were brought down from $130 million to $35 million. Others have experimented with AI features or used AI tools to help with things like audio syncing. Kathleen Kennedy, who served as the president of Lucasfilm from 2012 to 2026, helped organize a group of industry dignitaries to put together a framework for how Hollywood should talk about it.

“When you have a set of tools that all of a sudden, ‘I can dream it, and I can create it, and I can show it to somebody,’ what you realize is that it heightens your creativity and did not diminish it at all,” Erwin says.

But even with such attitudinal strides, Pew Research shows that people’s fears about AI’s societal impact are high, and digital choirs hurl insults at any project featuring the tech. It’s led creatives to walk a tricky line between the wish to experiment with AI and the havoc disclosing its use can wreak.

“If the creative is great and it engages the audience on a different level than just ‘Hey, look at this thing that’s AI,’ the audience is going to understand it,” says Kathleen Grace, Lionsgate’s chief AI officer. “But it’s challenging when you lead with AI as the only hook.”

Some directors have gone all in. Oscar-winning director Steven Soderbergh sparked discourse earlier this year when he revealed how he used roughly 10 minutes of AI in his upcoming documentary “John Lennon: The Lost Interview.” He also disclosed his plans to use AI in his Wagner Moura-starring film about the Spanish-American War.

While Soderbergh recognizes AI remains a “very emotional subject,” he says the loudest voices raging against its use are those that haven’t bothered to engage with it at all. “I’ve seen the version of the John Lennon doc without that material, and I’ve seen the version with the material that we generated, and the version with that material is a better version of the movie,” Soderbergh says. “Here’s what’s really funny to me: If I told people that nine minutes and 40 seconds was VFX that took two and a half million dollars in two years, there would have been no debate at all. So what are we talking about?”

It’s a mindset that “Bourne Identity” director Liman brought to “Bitcoin,” an upcoming Casey Affleck and Gal Gadot-led picture tracing a man’s quest to prove he invented the controversial currency. The project recruited Acme, which specializes in “gray box” soundstages that host real humans while a team of 150 AI artists generates the location imagery and lighting.

Liman, according to Jed Weintrob, the CEO of Liman’s content studio 30 Ninjas, “likes to push the envelope” and thinks AI tools can be “real superchargers for storytellers.” “We’re creating a world that would be almost financially impossible to make without this technology,” he says.

Kavanaugh claims the industry shift toward embracing AI was caused by Liman’s decision to go public with his use of it. After the initial disclosure, Acme took several meetings with a mix of studios and filmmakers eager to understand how a project managed to dramatically lower costs. (Kavanaugh wouldn’t disclose the names of the group.)

After those meetings, Kavanaugh says, the creatives realized that “we’re not killing the art; we’re enhancing the art.“ He adds, “It’s making it more efficient. It’s creating better tool sets. And all of a sudden, we really saw a big shift … from people that we thought were going to be like, ‘No, we can’t do that,’ to ‘Well, can we use it in this show?’”

Still, such curiosity doesn’t mean all-encompassing acceptance — either by the industry or the audiences that sustain it. This summer alone saw the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences disqualify synthetic performers and AI-written scripts from awards consideration, while the Cannes Film Festival issued a blanket ban on AI-generated productions. When the Urbanworld Film Festival said in June it would accept AI-generated productions for its 30th edition, the Writers Guild of America ended its long-standing sponsorship. The move was consistent with the union’s concerns about the improper use of AI, but it was a choice Urbanworld CEO Stacy Spikes says risks creating a “very slippery slope” — after all, should anyone dictate what tools aspiring filmmakers can experiment with?

Actors have taken action against the harmful effects of AI. Soderbergh endorsed the Human Consent Foundation, a nonprofit cofounded by Cate Blanchett in June, that created a database where people are encouraged to register how their likenesses can or can’t be pulled by AI models. Blanchett told Variety at the time that while the registry may not revolutionize how people engage with AI, “the more people adopt it, the more chance it has of making a real impact.” She added, “We do have to start somewhere, because thoughtlessness is the enemy of creativity.”

Audiences have also revolted against AI’s intersection with Hollywood, criticizing the initially undisclosed use of the technology for a sequence in Eli Roth’s horror film “Ice Cream Man” and a marketing campaign featuring podcasting dogs for Warner Bros. Discovery’s “The End of Oak Street.”

Jeffrey Katzenberg, the veteran Hollywood executive who wrote a 2,377-word essay on X last month urging the film industry to work with Silicon Valley and responsibly adopt the technology, says he’s noticed a pervasive sense of “concern and fear” surrounding AI’s presence in Hollywood. The resistance mimics what he calls a pattern of averting “innovation and change.” But, he warns, “to resist technology is to risk irrelevance.”

Katzenberg is entering the fray himself, developing an AI animation studio that will serve as a vehicle for tools he thinks the industry can adopt. But he hopes to also create a project that could spur a true sentiment shift in the way “Toy Story,” created by his former studio Pixar, did for CGI in the ’90s. “We’ll all know when we see it,” Katzenberg says. “Tools are never the point. What matters is taste, creativity and imagination.”

For Hollywood to progress, Katzenberg says, it has to accept the wave of change — and progress — AI can bring. It’s part of the ethos of his AI animation studio, capitalizing on what he sees as “a true renaissance for Hollywood storytelling” and “a complete transformation of all forms of video creation.”

Walking the tightrope between acceptance and resistance puts studios, eager to save money with AI, in a bind. How do you greenlight original stories that may use AI when faced with audiences and creatives wary of the technology? “I don’t really know,” one AI-adopting studio executive admits.

But a lot of people’s consternation, the executive says, comes from how U.S. political leaders and tech executives are handling the messaging surrounding AI and fears around its impact on jobs, a factor those in Hollywood have little control over. “Right now, the political context of it would be “Well, gee, if you used AI, you displace people’s jobs. You would have hired 1,000 people rather than 100,’” the executive says. “Yeah, that’s probably true.” But, he claims, studios can now make 10 times as many projects due to the efficiency of AI. And more projects will ultimately amount to the same number of people working. No one can argue with the fact that the industry will benefit from having more stories to tell.

Hollywood’s next battle? Getting the AI-powered work produced by industry professionals to resonate with audiences, as opposed to the online video slop made by people without industry experience.

“The reality is the excellence that you see in cinematic storytelling is because there are creators, directors, filmmakers, costume designers, production designers,” the executive says. “They think very deeply [about] what that experience is going to be. The people creating the slop have not thought deeply about it.”

Spikes说,风险创造了一个“非常滑动的脚踏板” - 毕竟,应该有人说什么工具希望电影制作人可以尝试?", "links": [{"text": "disqualify", "url": "https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/oscars-rules-2027-ai-actors-screenplays-international-1236581862/"}, {"text": "blanket ban", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/features/i-saw-hell-grind-ai-generated-film-cannes-shocking-realistic-1236770720/"}, {"text": "accept", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/news/urbanworld-festival-accept-ai-films-30th-anniversary-1236781077/"}, {"text": "says", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/biz/news/urbanworld-ceo-stacy-spikes-interview-wga-sponsorship-ai-1236824517/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Soderbergh 赞成了人文同意基金会,非营利基金会由 Cate Blanchett 于 6 月共同创立,该基金会创建了一个数据库,人们被鼓励记录他们的相似之处如何可以或不能被人工智能模型吸引。无思是创造力的敌人。", "links": [{"text": "can or can’t", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/biz/news/cate-blanchett-steven-soderbergh-nikki-hexum-ai-human-registry-1236791271/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "观众也反对人工智能与好莱坞的交叉,批评最初未透露的技术使用在Eli Roth的恐怖片“冰淇淋男子”和一个营销活动,包含Podcasting狗为华纳兄弟发现的“Oak街的终结”。", "links": [{"text": "criticizing", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/biz/news/urbanworld-ceo-stacy-spikes-interview-wga-sponsorship-ai-1236824517/"}, {"text": "marketing campaign", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/news/warner-bros-ai-dog-podcast-the-end-of-oak-street-1236830713/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Jeffrey Katzenberg,老年好莱坞执行官谁写了一篇 2,377字的论文上月X呼吁电影行业与硅谷合作,并负责任采用技术,他说他注意到一个突破性的感觉“对抗和恐惧”围绕人工智能在好莱坞的存在。", "links": [{"text": "essay", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/biz/news/jeffrey-katzenberg-hollywood-must-accept-not-going-away-1236873535/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "卡森伯格正在进入自己,开发一个人工智能动画工作室,将作为工具的工具,他认为行业可以采用,但他希望也创造一个项目,可以引发真正的情感转变的方式“玩具故事”,由他的前工作室Pixar创建,为CGI在90年代。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "为了好莱坞取得进展,卡森伯格说,它必须接受变革的浪潮 - 和进步 - 人工智能可以带来它是他的人工智能动画工作室的道德的一部分,资本化他所看到的“好莱坞故事的真正复兴”和“所有形式的视频创作的完整转变”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "走在接受和抵抗之间的紧张线,将工作室,渴望用人工智能节省资金,放在一个连接中。 如何使用人工智能当面对观众和创造者对技术的警惕时,可以绿灯的原创故事? “我真的不知道,”一个人工智能采用工作室的执行官承认。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但是,许多人的焦虑,执行官说,来自美国的政治领袖和技术执行官如何处理人工智能周围的信息和担心它对就业的影响,一个因素,好莱坞的人对它有很少的控制,“现在,它的政治背景会是“好,说,如果你使用人工智能,你取代人们的工作。 1,000 人而不是 100 ”““执行官说,“是的,这很可能是真的。但,他声称,研究所现在可以做 10 时间如由于人工智能的效率,很多项目最终会相当于同一数量的人工作,没有人可以争论,行业将受益于拥有更多的故事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "好莱坞的下一场战斗? 让行业专业人士制作的人工智能工作与观众相反,与没有行业经验的人在线视频拍摄相反。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“现实是你在电影故事中看到的卓越是因为有创作者,导演,电影制作人,服装设计师,制作设计师,”执行官说,“他们非常深思熟虑(关于)这个体验将是什么。", "translated": true}]

2025年在 Matca 上发表，并可能随后在 Writing Foto 上发表。获得者将获得 10,000,000 VND 的专业稿酬，以及来自 Matca 团队与客座导师庄武彬的编辑指导和翻译支持。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "申请时，请提交一份关于 2 至 5 2025年完成，若有需要，可预留额外的翻译和出版时间。所有在 Matca 上发表的文本都将提供越南语和英语双语版本。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如果常驻河内，获得者还可以完全使用 Matca 的图书馆进行研究，并可以提议撰写一篇针对该馆藏的回应文章。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "申请资格：", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "面向所有国籍的写作者。个人和集体均可申请。申请者的常驻地不限，但应具备对越南语境下摄影的扎实理解。文章可以使用越南语、英语或两者皆有。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "如果您有任何进一步的问题，请随时联系 hello@matca.vn 。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "关于客座导师", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Trương Quế Chi 是一位工作生活于河内的艺术家兼策展人。她的实践横跨雕塑装置、电影和戏剧等不同领域，同时对比例、材料、节奏和时间性保持高度关注。作为对社会、历史及自传性事件和结构的抽象呈现，Quế Chi 的作品深入探索了日常生活的奇观、其对照的情感以及其中的谜团。近期，Chi 一直与艺术家 Nguyen Phuong Linh 合作，参加了 2024 年釜山双年展和 2024 年亚洲艺术双年展。自 2015 年起，她一直担任 Nhà Sàn Collective 的策展委员会成员。", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "庄武斌是一位从事摄影、出版和展览创作的写作者。他拥有伦敦威斯敏斯特大学的已发表作品博士学位（研究-摄影）。庄武斌是 2018 年度何鸿毅家族基金大中华研究资助金的主要获得者，也是克劳斯亲王基金研究资助金（2010 年）的获得者。在新加坡，庄武斌获得了国家图书馆（NL）2023 年度数字奖学金以及新加坡国家图书馆 2017 年度李光前研究奖学金。他曾受邀参加万隆理工学院（2013 年）、香港亚洲艺术文献库（AAA）（2015 年）、台湾关渡美术馆（2017 年）以及亚洲艺术文献库的夏碧泉档案项目（2018 年）的研究驻留计划。他是清迈摄影节的特约策展人（2015 年、2017 年、2020 年）。由新加坡国立大学出版社出版的《东南亚摄影：一项调查》（2016 年）是他的第四本书。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://matca.vn/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/matca_grant_2025_web_ENG_001-1024x682.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Matca"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "MATCA CREATION GRANT 2025"}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Deadline for submissions: 08.06.2025 via the form", "links": [{"text": "form", "url": "https://forms.gle/zxcf5Zy86fg71jtB6"}]}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Recipients announced: 30.06.2025"}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Project duration: July – December 2025"}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Be a patron: If you would like to join us in nurturing independent voices in Vietnam’s photography, kindly contact hello@matca.vn."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In 2021, we launched the first Creation Grant in response to the pandemic and the ongoing precarity faced by Vietnamese photographers. The inaugural awardee, Vu Khoi Nguyen, received funding and mentorship to realize his first documentary project on the fading tradition of coal carving rooted in his hometown’s industrial heritage. After six months, he presented his work-in-progress in an open studio and has continued working in photography ever since."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Over nine years of community work, we have encountered many emerging voices like Nguyen: often self-taught, deeply curious and observant, yet lacking sustained support for professional growth. While Vietnam’s landscape is quickly evolving, opportunities to create, exhibit, and publish photography remain persistently limited. As an independent, photographer-run initiative, we have established the Creation Grant as a way to pay it forward. Our principle is simple: when each plays a part, we can spark projects that, though modest in scale, leave a lasting impact on their communities. Starting small, starting local, starting now."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The second round of the Matca Creation Grant supports the production of one photography exhibition and one series of texts from July to December 2025. This time, we are delighted to have artist, curator Trương Quế Chi (VN) and writer, researcher Zhuang Wubin (SG) who will join us as guest mentors."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "What we offer:"}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Two cash prizes of 10,000,000 VND each"}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Artistic, editorial and logistics support from the Matca team and guest mentors"}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Exhibition and publication opportunities"}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Extensive promotion through all of our platforms"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "01. Exhibition grant"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "This grant supports one Vietnamese photographer or collective in exhibiting their work at Matca Space for Photography, which will run for 4-6 weeks within July-October. They receive a flat fee of 10,000,000 VND, free use of a 40m² fully equipped space in central Hanoi, artistic and logistical guidance to shape their presentation, and promotion through press and public-facing events. The awardee will work closely with the Matca team and guest mentor Trương Quế Chi."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Applicants should submit a ready-to-exhibit body of work or one near completion. Alongside images, they should include a rough proposal about the exhibition concept at our space. The proposal should specify the number of images intended for display, materials and presentation format (e.g., paper type, framing or unframed), and additional elements such as text, signage, or interactive components, if any. This information will help us understand the scope of the exhibition, but it is subject to change based on suitability and feasibility."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "If based outside Hanoi, the awardee is expected to cover their own costs to attend the installation, opening, and artist talk."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Eligibility:"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Open to Vietnamese nationals based in Vietnam, excluding the Vietnamese diaspora. Individuals and collectives can apply. No restrictions on the topic or genre of photography."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "02. Writing grant"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "This grant supports one writer or collective in developing a series of writings on photography, to be published on Matca in 2025 and potentially later on Writing Foto. The grantee will receive a professional fee of 10,000,000 VND, along with editorial guidance and translation support from the Matca team and guest mentor Zhuang Wubin."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "To apply, please submit a pitch for a series of 2 to 5 articles that explore photography, either historical or contemporary, in relation to Vietnam. The texts can stand alone or form part of a thematic series, and may take the form of interviews, features, reviews, or analytical essays. While the pitch should clearly express the author’s interest and approach, there will be flexibility in shaping the final outputs during the development process."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "All work must be completed by 2025, with additional time allocated for translation and publication if needed. All texts published on Matca will be in both Vietnamese and English."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "If based in Hanoi, the grantee will also have full access to Matca’s library for research and may propose a written response to the collection."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Eligibility:"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Open to writers of all nationalities. Individuals and collectives can apply. Applicants can be based anywhere but should have a solid understanding of photography in Vietnam’s context. Writings may be in Vietnamese, English, or both."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Submission guidelines"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Via the form , applicants to both grants must submit the following documents before 18.05.2025: Proposal (max. 1,000 words), photography or writing portfolio (max. PDF size 25MB), biography and CV, and additional materials, if any.", "links": [{"text": "form", "url": "https://forms.gle/zxcf5Zy86fg71jtB6"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "There is no submission fee. Application forms and materials can be in either Vietnamese or English. The results will be announced via email by 30.06."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "If you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact hello@matca.vn ."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "About guest mentors"}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Trương Quế Chi is a Hanoi-based artist and curator. Her practice ​​​​traverses the borders of different terrains including sculptural installation, film, and theater, while remaining attentive to proportion, materials, rhythm and temporality. As abstract renderings of social, historical, and autobiographical events and structures, Quế Chi’s works delve into the spectacle of the everyday, its contrasting feelings, its enigma. Recently, Chi has been collaborating with artist Nguyen Phuong Linh, participating in the Busan Biennale 2024 and Asian Art Biennale 2024. Since 2015, she has been a curatorial board member of Nhà Sàn Collective."}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "Zhuang Wubin is a writer who makes photographs, publications and exhibitions. He received his PhD by Published Work (Research–Photography) from University of Westminster, London. Zhuang is the major grantee of Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation Greater China Research Grant 2018 and a recipient of the Prince Claus Fund research grant (2010). In Singapore, Zhuang is the recipient of the National Library (NL) Digital Fellowship 2023 and the Lee Kong Chian Research Fellowship 2017 at the NL. He has been invited to research residency programmes at Institute Technology of Bandung (2013), Asia Art Archive (AAA), Hong Kong (2015), Kuandu Museum of Fine Arts, Taiwan (2017) and the Ha Bik Chuen Archive Project at AAA (2018). He is the contributing curator of the Chiang Mai Photo Festival (2015, 2017, 2020). Published by NUS Press, Photography in Southeast Asia: A Survey (2016) is his fourth book."}]

MATCA CREATION GRANT 2025

Deadline for submissions: 08.06.2025 via the form

Recipients announced: 30.06.2025

Project duration: July – December 2025

Be a patron: If you would like to join us in nurturing independent voices in Vietnam’s photography, kindly contact hello@matca.vn.

In 2021, we launched the first Creation Grant in response to the pandemic and the ongoing precarity faced by Vietnamese photographers. The inaugural awardee, Vu Khoi Nguyen, received funding and mentorship to realize his first documentary project on the fading tradition of coal carving rooted in his hometown’s industrial heritage. After six months, he presented his work-in-progress in an open studio and has continued working in photography ever since.

Over nine years of community work, we have encountered many emerging voices like Nguyen: often self-taught, deeply curious and observant, yet lacking sustained support for professional growth. While Vietnam’s landscape is quickly evolving, opportunities to create, exhibit, and publish photography remain persistently limited. As an independent, photographer-run initiative, we have established the Creation Grant as a way to pay it forward. Our principle is simple: when each plays a part, we can spark projects that, though modest in scale, leave a lasting impact on their communities. Starting small, starting local, starting now.

The second round of the Matca Creation Grant supports the production of one photography exhibition and one series of texts from July to December 2025. This time, we are delighted to have artist, curator Trương Quế Chi (VN) and writer, researcher Zhuang Wubin (SG) who will join us as guest mentors.

What we offer:

Two cash prizes of 10,000,000 VND each

Artistic, editorial and logistics support from the Matca team and guest mentors

Exhibition and publication opportunities

Extensive promotion through all of our platforms

01. Exhibition grant

This grant supports one Vietnamese photographer or collective in exhibiting their work at Matca Space for Photography, which will run for 4-6 weeks within July-October. They receive a flat fee of 10,000,000 VND, free use of a 40m² fully equipped space in central Hanoi, artistic and logistical guidance to shape their presentation, and promotion through press and public-facing events. The awardee will work closely with the Matca team and guest mentor Trương Quế Chi.

Applicants should submit a ready-to-exhibit body of work or one near completion. Alongside images, they should include a rough proposal about the exhibition concept at our space. The proposal should specify the number of images intended for display, materials and presentation format (e.g., paper type, framing or unframed), and additional elements such as text, signage, or interactive components, if any. This information will help us understand the scope of the exhibition, but it is subject to change based on suitability and feasibility.

If based outside Hanoi, the awardee is expected to cover their own costs to attend the installation, opening, and artist talk.

Eligibility:

Open to Vietnamese nationals based in Vietnam, excluding the Vietnamese diaspora. Individuals and collectives can apply. No restrictions on the topic or genre of photography.

02. Writing grant

This grant supports one writer or collective in developing a series of writings on photography, to be published on Matca in 2025 and potentially later on Writing Foto. The grantee will receive a professional fee of 10,000,000 VND, along with editorial guidance and translation support from the Matca team and guest mentor Zhuang Wubin.

To apply, please submit a pitch for a series of 2 to 5 articles that explore photography, either historical or contemporary, in relation to Vietnam. The texts can stand alone or form part of a thematic series, and may take the form of interviews, features, reviews, or analytical essays. While the pitch should clearly express the author’s interest and approach, there will be flexibility in shaping the final outputs during the development process.

All work must be completed by 2025, with additional time allocated for translation and publication if needed. All texts published on Matca will be in both Vietnamese and English.

If based in Hanoi, the grantee will also have full access to Matca’s library for research and may propose a written response to the collection.

Eligibility:

Open to writers of all nationalities. Individuals and collectives can apply. Applicants can be based anywhere but should have a solid understanding of photography in Vietnam’s context. Writings may be in Vietnamese, English, or both.

Submission guidelines

Via the form , applicants to both grants must submit the following documents before 18.05.2025: Proposal (max. 1,000 words), photography or writing portfolio (max. PDF size 25MB), biography and CV, and additional materials, if any.

There is no submission fee. Application forms and materials can be in either Vietnamese or English. The results will be announced via email by 30.06.

If you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact hello@matca.vn .

About guest mentors

Trương Quế Chi is a Hanoi-based artist and curator. Her practice ​​​​traverses the borders of different terrains including sculptural installation, film, and theater, while remaining attentive to proportion, materials, rhythm and temporality. As abstract renderings of social, historical, and autobiographical events and structures, Quế Chi’s works delve into the spectacle of the everyday, its contrasting feelings, its enigma. Recently, Chi has been collaborating with artist Nguyen Phuong Linh, participating in the Busan Biennale 2024 and Asian Art Biennale 2024. Since 2015, she has been a curatorial board member of Nhà Sàn Collective.

Zhuang Wubin is a writer who makes photographs, publications and exhibitions. He received his PhD by Published Work (Research–Photography) from University of Westminster, London. Zhuang is the major grantee of Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation Greater China Research Grant 2018 and a recipient of the Prince Claus Fund research grant (2010). In Singapore, Zhuang is the recipient of the National Library (NL) Digital Fellowship 2023 and the Lee Kong Chian Research Fellowship 2017 at the NL. He has been invited to research residency programmes at Institute Technology of Bandung (2013), Asia Art Archive (AAA), Hong Kong (2015), Kuandu Museum of Fine Arts, Taiwan (2017) and the Ha Bik Chuen Archive Project at AAA (2018). He is the contributing curator of the Chiang Mai Photo Festival (2015, 2017, 2020). Published by NUS Press, Photography in Southeast Asia: A Survey (2016) is his fourth book.

article_text:
新体制で迎えた6回目。18の国と地域から63ギャラリーが集結

京都を舞台に「コラボレーション」を掲げる現代美術のアートフェア 「Art Collaboration Kyoto（ACK）」 が、11月7日から 国立京都国際会館 ほかで一般公開を迎えた。6回目となる今年は、複数のディレクターが共同でフェアを率いる「リーダーシップコミッティー」という新たな体制のもとで開催される。会期は11月9日まで。

出展するのは、18の国と地域の24都市から集まった63ギャラリーで、そのうち18ギャラリーが初出展となる。大型ブースへの応募が増えたことを受け、会場にはブースごとの個性を体感しやすい、スケールの大きな展示空間が用意された。会場デザインは今年も建築家の周防貴之（SUO）が担当。通路の延長にブースが現れ、通路にも作品があふれ出すような構成によって、来場者は会場全体をひとつの大きな展示として巡ることができる。

ゲストキュレーターにレオナルド・バルトロメウス。企画展示「Intersections」が問う「境界の外へ」

ブースの外に広がるスペースで展開される企画展示「Intersections」では、 山口情報芸術センター［YCAM］ のキュレーター、レオナルド・バルトロメウスがゲストキュレーターを務める。掲げたテーマは「境界の外へ」。知らないうちに引かれた境界線や、暗黙のルールに囲まれて暮らす現代において、アートがその先へどう踏み出せるのかを問いかける。参加作家は、エフライン・アルメイダ、金氏徹平、ピオトレク・コワルスキー、クリス・レムサル、松平莉奈、エルネスト・ネト、大野綾子、大田黒衣美、鈴木祥太、リア・ケ・イー・ジェン（鄭柯顗）の10名で、作品はすべて購入することもできる。

海外ギャラリーとブースを分け合う。カナダから初参加の組み合わせも

ACKの柱となるのは、国内のギャラリーが海外のギャラリーを招き、ひとつのブースを共有する「ギャラリーコラボレーション」と、京都にゆかりのある作家や作品を紹介する「キョウトミーティング」のふたつのセクションだ。今年のギャラリーコラボレーションでは、国内の25ギャラリーがホストとなり、海外の27ギャラリーを迎える。 TARO NASU とHauser & Wirth（チューリッヒ）、ナンヅカとジェフリー・ダイチ（ニューヨーク）、 東京画廊＋BTAP とGallery Hyundai（ソウル）など、初出展のギャラリーを含む組み合わせが並ぶ。 キョウトミーティングには国内の6ギャラリーと海外の5ギャラリーが参加し、 Perrotin 、Mendes Wood DM、 SCAI THE BATHHOUSE 、 ShugoArts などが、京都ならではの展示を見せる。

カナダ・バンクーバーのUnit 17を迎えた KOKI ARTS は、ACKの創設時から参加してきたギャラリーで、今回は2年ぶりの出展となる。両ギャラリーは2年ほど前に東京のアートフェアで知り合い、アートフェアへの関わり方や今後の展望に共通点が多かったことから、今回のコラボレーションに至った。ブースで紹介するのは、京都を拠点とする中屋敷智生と、トロントを拠点とするエラ・ゴンザレスのふたり。国籍も世代も異なり、互いに面識もないふたりだが、出展の申請書類を準備するなかで、マスキングテープを重ねて画面に層を生む中屋敷と、家族のスナップ写真や3Dモデルをもとに描くゴンザレスの作品が、「重なり」をめぐって対話することにあらためて気づかされたという。

宮永愛子、岡﨑龍之祐、新プログラム「NEW STREAM」。パートナー企業との「スペシャルプログラム」

パートナー企業6社との協働による「スペシャルプログラム」では、宮永愛子が「金」の記憶と時間をめぐるインスタレーション「What Gold Becomes」（株式会社SGC）を発表。大丸松坂屋百貨店による次世代アーティスト支援「Ladder Project」からは迎英里子の新作を、髙島屋との企画では岡﨑龍之祐による布を用いた彫刻群「THE BODY RETURNS TO」を紹介する。

ジンテックの支援により新たに始動する「NEW STREAM」は、気鋭のアーティストを京都へ招き、継続的な支援の循環を生むことを目指す取り組みだ。初回は井上七海、川田知志、キム・ジェフン、衣川明子、坂本紬野子が参加する。このほか、桑山との企画「ジュエリー：身の上のものがたり」では、サイモン・フジワラら国内外の作家によるコンテンポラリージュエリーが並ぶ。

若手アーティストを支援するシャンパーニュ ポメリーのアワード「Pommery Prize Kyoto」も継続し、今年のファイナリストである松岡日菜子、岡田摩耶、リュ・ジェユンの3名の作品をVIPラウンジで展示する。またVIPプログラムでは、東邦レオがアーティストのシアスター・ゲイツとともに、屋外テラスに「待合室」を設えている。

是枝裕和×川村元気のトークに、子供向けワークショップも。京都の街へ広がるACK

国立京都国際会館ニューホールで開かれる「ACK Talks」では、人と人とのつながりや、思想と美学の継承をキーワードに、会期中に計8本のセッションを実施する。初日の7日には京都府知事の西脇隆俊と建築家の妹島和世が都市と文化について語り、8日にはアーティストで映画監督のアーサー・ジャファが登壇。最終日の9日には、映画監督の是枝裕和と映画プロデューサー・小説家の川村元気による「Kyoto Dialogue」が予定されている。トークは予約不要の先着順で、同時通訳がつく（入場にはACKチケットが必要）。

バンコクの文化施設「Bangkok Kunsthalle」と共同で立ち上げた「Bangkok Collaborate Kyoto Fellowship（BCK Fellowship）」も継続し、ACKの出展アーティストのなかから、バンコクでのレジデンスと展覧会の機会を得る受賞者を選ぶ。結果は8日の授賞式で発表される。

子供向けの「Kids’ Programs」では、美術作家の河野愛、桶職人の中川周士、アーティストの荒木悠と腹話術師の山田春江を講師に迎え、日替わりでワークショップを実施。副産物産店による「キッズスタジオ」も毎日オープンし、生後3ヶ月から小学2年生までを対象にした日英バイリンガルの託児サービスも用意されている（いずれも参加無料、ワークショップと託児は要事前申込）。

会期中は京都市内各所でも展覧会やアートイベントが開かれており、ACKはそれらを「What’s On」として紹介している。新善光寺でのポピー・ジョーンズ展、 有斐斎弘道館 での ミリアム・カーン展 、 タカ・イシイギャラリー 京都 での アダム・ペンドルトン展 など、寺院や町家を舞台にした展示も多い。京都府と京都市が進める「京都アート月間」とも連携し、市内のイベントを結ぶシャトルバスも運行される。紅葉が色づき始めた京都の街を、フェア会場とあわせて巡ってみてほしい。

Commons”之后的第二弹。近年来，以游戏为主题的展览日益增多，而本展所重视的视角不仅在于将游戏视为体验的媒介，更将目光投向了各个游戏作品所涉及的主题及其背后的个人、社会经验与结构。藤本特别指出，在被称为“酷儿游戏”的作品中，游戏内的规则与现实社会的规则是如何相连的，是一个重要切入点。", "links": [{"text": "「Under Commons」", "url": "据藤本介绍，“酷儿游戏”是指通过游戏游玩过程，对各种社会规范、性与性别规范提出质问的作品。此外，它也带有“小型游戏”（藤本受近藤银河的研究词汇启发而使用）的含义，如同第三波女性主义中的 ZINE 一样，将个人的实在及其痕迹作为档案传递出去。不过，他也表示，本展中涉及的游戏并非全部都由开发者自身冠以“酷儿游戏”之名。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/8fd5aa1a/965ac462-7425-4187-9cbc-78b9fa81ad78.JPG?q=70&fm=webp", "alt": "", "caption": "展览主视觉海报出自吉约姆·桑瑞兰（Guillaume Singelin），他曾负责本展参展游戏《Citizen Sleeper》的角色设计与视觉工作。海报描绘了展览主题“获取”以及游戏与当代艺术交融的世界", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本次展览以“获取”为关键词，实现了独立游戏作品与当代艺术家的合作。在展厅中，远藤麻衣、大石一贵、清原启这3位艺术家分别试玩了不同的游戏，并根据这些体验，展出了将各游戏的根本主题、规则及创作背景等进行转译的艺术作品。此外，现场还展出了全球热门独立游戏作品的介绍以及美国艺术家菲内根·施农（Finnegan Shannon）的作品。另外，在游戏选择方面，《Analogue: A Hate Story》由藤本挑选，其余游戏则由高岛挑选。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在本展中，艺术家与游戏开发者通过两个侧面紧密相连：“作品／游戏本身成为通往某种现实或知识的获取工具”；同时，“当历史或社会的结构性壁垒阻碍了某些人的选择即获取可能性时，作品／游戏也成为了将其揭露出来的分析工具”。接下来，我们将结合藤本的话语一同参观展厅。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/fdf6bc92/5a1bb3eb-c56f-42cc-a796-c6daba7d8ed6.JPG?q=70&fm=webp", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，右侧为菲内根·施农《Time travel with me》（2022,2026）", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展厅分为免费区域与收费区域，入口附近的免费区域由菲内根·施农的展示迎接着来访者。通过作品与艺术实践探索各种“获取”形态的施农，于2022年发表了作品《Time travel with me》，游走于作为无障碍工具的语音导览与作品边界之间。本项目为本次展览重新构筑了将整个展览的视觉信息转化为语言并录音的内容，此次通过耳机播放参展艺术家清原、远藤和大石的声音，讲述各自的展示内容、作品概念以及在何处、以何种方式展示了什么。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "免费区域的另一个企划是选书专区。在人文書院与 Katabami Shobo 的协助下，3位艺术家与近藤银河从两家出版社的出版物中挑选了有助于更深入理解展览的书籍。各作家的展示展位上也放置了各自的选书，均可在现场购买。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/d80dfa44/e1dee64e-a655-4cf9-8d0c-c0f634eaf739.JPG?q=70&fm=webp", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，选书专区", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "3位当代艺术家深入试玩游戏并将其转译为作品", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "收费区域从艺术家与游戏的合作展位开始。在与游戏合作时，给予艺术家的共同方针不是二次使用游戏内角色等表象，而是提取出游戏的规则或根本主题这一“核心”来创作作品。因此，展示乍一看可能与游戏没有直接的关联。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "第一位艺术家是清原启，他通过记忆、笔记和速写，将突发的人际交往、偏离行为等绘成绘画。他游玩的是以被资本主义彻底吞噬的未来宇宙为舞台的科幻 RPG《Citizen Sleeper》（Jump Over The Age，2022）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/984b5797/68449a34-587e-4112-a3d7-c05762b00792.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，清原启的展示", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "清原绘制在画布或画纸上的绘画与素描中，映现出他在日常生活中瞥见的人们的偶然姿态，如在超市或车站见到的人、空调安装工等。画作中用文字描绘了那个人的样貌、言语以及当天发生的事件等，从中浮现出作为生活者与劳动者生存于现代日本社会的人们的面貌。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/a6271d42/9dbed53b-b28f-41f7-980f-bd45536dc956.JPG", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，清原启的展示", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一方面，在《Citizen Sleeper》中，玩家化身为被称为“Sleeper”的“拟似生命体”，在寻找于旧宇宙飞船中生存之道的同时，通过与他人对话、传递物品来建立关系。玩家可以自由行动，但能执行的行为受限于骰子的点数。艺术家将这一点与市场原理的特征重叠起来——即人们以为是自己情愿做出的选择，其实也是被外部因素所挑选的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在被编入市场原理的过程中，人们如何向其发起挑战、经历失败并找到出路？藤本表示，正是因为根基处存在着这样的质问，清原的作品与《Citizen Sleeper》才产生了共鸣。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/2cdd920d/d550844d-6043-460f-9f77-e840d3bed637.JPG", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，前方为 Jump Over The Age《Citizen Sleeper》的游玩画面", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "以“身体的政治性”为主题、通过与他人的共同作业进行创作的远藤麻衣，其合作的游戏是科幻游戏《Analogue: A Hate Story》（Love Conquers All Games，2012）。该游戏讲述了这样一个故事：在李氏朝鲜时代的父 patriarchal 文化复权的“未来”无人宇宙船中醒来的主角，一边解读死者留下的日志，一边通过黑客技术入侵父权制与婚姻制度并改写代码，让消逝于历史中的无名女性的声音浮现出来。著有《失败的酷儿艺术──泛滥的动画》等书的杰克·哈尔伯斯特姆（Jack Halberstam）将该作作为“酷儿游戏”进行了论述，并赞赏了其将未被写入家谱的女性写入其中、通过改写代码来打破法律与习俗的类比。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/e2b7fcb0/72cb850d-2756-406f-941b-a8343e3d7702.JPG", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，Love Conquers All Games《Analogue: A Hate Story》的游玩画面", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "面对这部试图想象并复权在男性中心文化中消失之人的存在与声音的作品，远藤以柳田国男的《先祖的故事》等为线索（该书提出了将未留下子孙便战死沙场的年轻人作为新家族的始祖进行供奉的建议），确立了“如何重新悼念国家级暴力所带来的大规模死亡”这一质问。在新作影像作品《当蹄声与芬芳渐渐隐去》（2026）中，她通过从无幻能获得启示的行为艺术，提出了与被国家作为英灵刻下名字不同的、另一种形式的悼念仪式。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/0881b6e9/13469fdc-95dd-4337-8d2f-e935e7ecb6fb.JPG", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，远藤麻衣《当蹄声与芬芳渐渐隐去》（2026）", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "大石一贵关注人类经验的碎片化同步以及唤起这种同步的物理现象，其创作横跨多种媒介，并以自己设定规则制作的雕刻作品而闻名。他游玩的游戏《The Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood》（Deconstructeam，2023）内容为：玩家化身为流放至小行星的占卜师女巫，一边用自己制作的塔罗牌占卜未来，一边左右着女巫社会的命运。该作具有借助占卜力量“改写”过去或未来的侧面，这暗示了面对具有非线性时间性的酷儿历史时，由自己重新构筑过去的种种可能性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/f74c919f/20a1b641-0e7d-4b5f-90f7-066e4257306a.JPG", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，Deconstructeam《The Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood》的游玩画面", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "大石根据游玩该作的经验，创作了作品《我来为你身上的裂纹占卜》，该作品以水黏土制作的台灯上的裂纹为基础进行占卜。大石预先为一条条不同的裂纹制作了53个剧本，将剧本上的言语套用到台灯的裂纹上进行占卜，并将结果写入面板中，与实际的台灯一同展出。藤本谈到，这种乍看之下似乎有些随意的占卜裂纹的行为，通过直面并对话于臆想以及刻在台灯上的面孔，逐渐巩固了台灯的实在性，这一过程与《The Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood》的游玩体验重叠在了一起。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/d6384777/5172df5c-08e1-41e4-8cbc-6bd99059b60b.JPG", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，大石一贵《我来为你身上的裂纹占卜》（2026）", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/67f80a79/bd0f58f8-bb36-48bf-a8ae-cf508423e631.JPG", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，大石一贵《我来为你身上的裂纹占卜》（局部）（2026）", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "游玩全球热门独立游戏及追溯酷儿痕迹的游戏", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "除此之外，除了与艺术家的合作之外，还有直接展示游戏本身的展品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "俄罗斯出身的尼基塔·克留科夫（Nikita Kryukov）的作品《Milk inside a bag of milk inside a bag of milk》（2020）内容很简单：一个少女去买牛奶，但从前往商店直到到达店里，购物过程并不顺利。这是一款视觉小说作品，配合着波普且复古的画风，让人们重新体验到许多人日常生活中微不足道的行为，对某些人而言究竟会伴随着多大的困难。该作品在日本也有人制作同人艺术等，享有极高的人气，此次与续集《Milk outside a bag of milk outside a bag of milk》（2021）一同展出。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/2d2d13fc/dfb568d3-d33b-4c8c-942e-1896a4ea38d6.JPG", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，尼基塔·克留科夫《Milk outside a bag of milk outside a bag of milk》的游玩画面", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "同样参与制作了《The Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood》的 Deconstructeam 推出的《Behind Every Great One》（2019）是一款扮演“伟大艺术家的妻子”并体验家务劳动的游戏。这也是一款简单的游戏，但游玩后就会发现无法从任何一扇门走出屋外。发生的事件包括做饭、打扫，以及应付那些发牢骚或要求性行为的丈夫等家庭内部的隐性劳动（Shadow Work）。由于如果不能顺利操持家务，主人公就会被逼入绝境，因此“玩好游戏”与“做好家务”重合在了一起，是一款相当令人感到不快的游戏。藤本称，这种强烈的体验正是该作的本质。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/d4619261/e91ae489-44d9-46d0-9c77-58af4a019f29.JPG", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，Deconstructeam《Behind Every Great One》的游玩画面", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最后是近藤银河的作品《Trace of Queer》（2026），他曾担任本展第1弾的客座策展人，也因从女性主义与酷儿视角批评游戏的著书《女权主义者，打游戏》而闻名。放置在展厅中央的本作是一款游戏，作者与其同为轮椅使用者的主人公在其中追寻着酷儿人群的痕迹。玩家通过在街道中与“生灵”相遇并对话，或者自身化为“生灵”，来寻找在公共空间与美术历史中被抹去的酷儿痕迹。在这一过程中，玩家也将直面诸如展厅只有楼梯而无法观看展览等城市的无障碍问题。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/c96356e5/ee907052-f1b2-4b02-92fc-187ab20c9728.JPG", "alt": "", "caption": "展厅现场，近藤银河《Trace of Queer》的游玩画面", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "藤本对该作评价道：“在酷儿人群的历史被主流历史排除在外的背景下，我认为这是一部抓住了‘酷儿游戏’核心的作品——它利用游戏这一媒介来重构历史，将其打造成可游玩的历史。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "游玩不自由，游戏的规则向现实中渗透", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本展中展示的游戏均可在现场游玩。虽然并不一定都是能轻松游玩的游戏，但藤本表示，体验游玩游戏的困难之处同样至关重要。玩家在几款游戏中感受到的不自由并非单纯的游戏设定，而是现实的不自由反映在游戏规则中的结果。“让人们去接触难以接触的困难（Access to difficulty）”也是本展的隐藏主题。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“当玩家与游戏内的规则发生碰撞，体验到那种不自由或不讲理时，就会意识到我们平时当作理所当然接受的现实社会规则同样绝非不证自明。创造出这种体验，正是‘酷儿游戏’的重要特征之一。”（藤本）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "藤本表示，希望今后能继续举办第3弹、第4弹。他谈了自己的展望，希望能够推进日语中尚属少见的与“酷儿游戏研究”相关的文献翻译工作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览中介绍的游戏不同于采用高精度 3DCG 的大型游戏，其特征在于保留了模拟触感的设计。仅接触丰富多样的独立游戏便已足够引人入胜，但在本展中，通过实际的游戏游玩以及艺术家们以自身视角将该体验进行转译的作品群，游戏向现实社会发出的质问也浮出水面。游戏作为一种能够接触多样视角与经验、重新审视现实的媒介。为了亲身体验这种可能性，希望大家能留出充裕的现场游玩时间前去参观。", "translated": true}]
